name: Access to Justice
title: Agentic AI and the future of justice: who will exercise judgement?
description: The legal profession has spent the last two years grappling with generative AI. The next challenge could be far more significant.On 5 October 2026, The Law Society published The Future of Agentic AI in the Justice System, examining how increasingly autonomous AI systems could reshape courts, tribunals and dispute resolution in England and Wales. Its central message is that a series of seemingly incremental decisions about technology and system design could gradually alter how justice is delivered and where authority sits within the system. This is a message that has filtered out of most legal conference panels on AI this year.Unlike conventional generative AI, which responds to prompts, agentic AI is designed to pursue objectives. It can interpret goals, plan actions and carry out a series of tasks with limited human intervention. While fully agentic systems are not yet being used within the justice system of England and Wales, the Law Society argues that the conditions for their emergence are already developing.
